rationale: Both offer well structured five-workshop series with timed agendas, a deliverable per session and persistent-canvas facilitation notes, and their overall arcs are very similar. A's explicit facilitation-technique column and its red-team, run-of-show and A/B hypothesis cards are nice touches. However, several of A's agendas exceed the stated three hours, and success metrics only appear in the final session. B shows stronger design judgment. It sets success metrics in Workshop 1 so later sessions can be traced to goals. It builds outside validation into the async plan (stakeholder interviews to check personas, message testing with five target users), so the strategy is not built purely on internal opinion. It includes engineering for launch constraints, a page-by-page content gap walk of the actual site, a pre-mortem for contingency, a decision log and explicit pivot triggers. It also advises when to merge sessions for small teams. B's agendas leave slack rather than overrunning. Overall B is the slightly sounder and more actionable facilitation design.
